study.question: Observation: the complete auxiliary-task ownership factorial gives all=0.6684156159937658 and none=0.6678548720585206; cart-only=0.6676098795854951, fav-only=0.6675955387475491, buy-only=0.6675472255081946, cart+fav=0.6679415531643654, cart+buy=0.668062300376734 and fav+buy=0.6672616258436628. All three single-task transfers underperform none, while all tasks outperform every subset; the all-minus-best-subset gap is 0.0003533156170317797. These are same-seed optimization outcomes, not independent confirmations of synergy. Does the useful all-task signed-product transfer require gradients into both encoded user identity and the remaining supplied context fields, or can a field-restricted transfer improve click AUC at identical learned capacity?
study.hypothesis: Provisional mechanism: auxiliary product-conditioned learning of shared context embeddings depends jointly on identity and nonidentity context. The identity edge can capture repeated-user associations while other context edges provide shared conditional structure; both together should outperform either isolated edge group with a positive two-factor AUC interaction. This is a hypothesis about the tested optimization pathway, not established memorization/generalization semantics. Restricting one group could instead remove interference and beat all, which would falsify joint necessity while offering a useful candidate. Earlier residual-branch field gates also favored all (0.6670575100016033) over identity-only (0.6668144964131157), other-only (0.6666226640621917) and none (0.6668051956575413); that different branch does not establish transfer to the product branch.

study.proposed_difference: A 2x2 factorial of auxiliary product-context input gradients: identity-only, other-only, all, none. All auxiliary task paths are enabled first. At training time only, split the already-embedded context in the existing self.user_fields order and detach disallowed field slices before the unchanged task context-query projection. All/none use identity and full detach fast paths; mixed cells concatenate unchanged values. Click and evaluation bypass the new gate. Projection parameters still learn from every task and all full-batch Dice populations remain native. Two candidates and two bridges are provided as independent standalone modules. No new learned parameters or persistent tensors; source-edge control is distinct from task loss removal or feature ablation. Product-branch joint necessity is unverified and no originality claim is made. Context widths must match the inherited fixed-width assumption, encoded user_id and at least one other context field must exist; violations are missing prerequisites, not scientific counterevidence. Actual dataset tensors/manifest are not exposed here; inherited host receipts and source hashes provide provenance but do not constitute fresh data verification. Latest knowledge-usage review: the prior round declared DIN inheritance and considered HeMix/OneTrans while rejecting expanded-ID capacity. Its four subset variants executed successfully, but all four underperform the all-task source. Successful execution verifies admissibility only; it does not prove a source-derived improvement or task cooperation mechanism. Current retrievals are assessed explicitly at top level; no original-method detail is silently inferred from a card or fallback.
predictions: At a shared parameter/buffer state every cell yields equal train/eval probabilities and native Dice updates. Every click Jacobian is unchanged; aux product-context field Jacobians follow the gates once zero output layers are opened for probes.

All and none should reproduce 0.6684156159937658 and 0.6678548720585206 under the frozen seed/recipe. These bridges check implementation; they add no independent mechanism repetition.

A restricted cell exceeding all and incumbent 0.668457307890924 is a predictive candidate requiring later paired-seed confirmation. Report all four tasks: the incumbent improves click over frozen sources but has lower auxiliary AUCs than DIN, so multi-task quality is not uniformly improved.

Use the existing empty, 1-16, 17-64 and >64 history bins without redefining them after outcomes; report sample, positive and negative counts, AUC/logloss and insufficient slices.
